newsitem.title: DENMARK: Denmark to focus on openness, environment at IGC.
newsitem.headline: Denmark to focus on openness, environment at IGC.

text.p: Denmark's government unveiled a draft policy document on Friday calling for tighter environmental legislation and more openness in the workings of the 15-member European Union (EU).
Setting out Denmark's latest thoughts on a reform of the workings of the EU, it is to be presented to the current IGC (intergovernmental conference) on the future of the bloc, the government said.
The IGC, which started in March, is due to complete its deliberations next year.
On environmental issues, the Danish government lists a four-point programme it intends to press for to gain inclusion in the final IGC pact.

It calls for EU to incorporate the targets of the 1992 Rio Conference on improving the global environment into its own treaty stipulations and pay more attention to environmental issues in all aspects of the bloc's activity.
Health, safety and environmental considerations must also be given greater priority in the single European market, the document said, and all EU member states should impose environmental taxes.

On openness, the Danish government said in its IGC draft that it would urge that transparency be laid down as one of the EU's basic principles in the new treaty, impinging on all aspects of the bloc's activity.
